content.text:
I have inspected every candidate location and searched the full document for audit-type rights. Findings:

- **sec-5 / §5–6 (Compensation, Documentation and Disputes)** — the only verification right runs *in our favour*: "Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged" and a right to contest charges. Fees are a monthly minimum plus scheduled charges, so TrueLink has no records-inspection hook.
- **sec-8 §8(f)** — TrueLink may "implement technical mechanisms" on its own hosted Interface to prevent spamming; this is an anti-spam enforcement right on TrueLink's own platform, not an audit, inspection or verification of Client records or systems.
- **sec-8 §9** — the only Client-granted access is "reasonable access" for TrueLink to make Y2K repairs/upgrades "at TrueLink's sole cost and expense", which benefits us.
- **sec-2 §3(e)** — usage statistics/log files flow *to* Client.
- No "audit", "inspect", "records", "examine" or "verify" language exists anywhere (all searches nil), and sec-1, sec-7, sec-10 and sec-12 (incl. all miscellaneous provisions) contain nothing responsive.

No audit right binding the Customer exists, so we sit better than the preferred position; inserting frequency/notice/cost limits would only imply an audit right that TrueLink does not currently have. No redline is warranted.

input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4), provided that Client timely pays all contested amounts.
input.rationale: The Agreement grants TrueLink no audit, inspection or verification right against Mortgage Logic.com. Compensation is a monthly minimum plus scheduled charges (§5(a)), and the only records/verification right in §6 runs in our favour (we receive supporting documentation and may contest charges); usage statistics and raw log files also flow to us under §3(e). Searches for audit, inspect, records, examine and verify return nothing anywhere in the document, and §§1, 2, 7, 10 and 12 contain no equivalent right. The two adjacent access-type provisions are not audit rights and are not adverse: §8(f) lets TrueLink implement technical anti-spam mechanisms on its own hosted Interface (no access to our records or systems), and §9 requires only "reasonable access" for TrueLink's Y2K repairs and upgrades "at TrueLink's sole cost and expense". With no audit right to constrain, we sit at or better than the preferred position (no frequency, notice, cost-shifting or system-access exposure), so no change is needed; proposing frequency/notice/cost limits would risk implying an audit right TrueLink does not have. We should resist any attempt to add one on renewal, and if TrueLink asks for verification rights we would require the preferred limits (annual, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site where possible, TrueLink's cost absent a 5% underpayment, no direct system access).
